why: These stories are bright wins for protecting habitats, from bought-and-saved estates to a wetland victory and a major conservation land deal.

steps: The trick: two little clues, one for each half of the word.

stories.headline: Big Save for Wooroora
stories.summary: A conservation group has raised over $19 million to buy and protect the Wooroora cattle station in far north Queensland.
key_points: More than $19m in private donations has been raised.
It lies about 100km south-west of Cairns and borders Yourka Reserve.
At least 12 threatened species have been recorded there.
stories.why_it_matters: Protecting this intact habitat helps safeguard rare wildlife, rainforest links, and country with deep cultural value for future generations.

stories.headline: Rothbury Fund Hits Goal
stories.summary: Campaigners have raised £30 million to buy the Rothbury estate in Northumberland and begin a major rewilding project.
key_points: The estate covers more than 3,800 hectares.
The campaign raised £30m, including £17m from the public.
The land is in Northumberland and was put up for sale two years ago.
stories.why_it_matters: Turning a huge estate into a nature recovery landscape shows how public support can restore habitats and reconnect wildlife across whole regions.

stories.headline: Fen Fight Wins Again
stories.summary: A Norfolk couple won another court case to protect Catfield Fen from pollution washing in from nearby arable fields.
key_points: The couple farm 460 acres in the Norfolk Broads.
Lady Justice Lieven ruled Natural England failed its duty.
Catfield Fen holds 2,500 species, including fen orchid and breeding bittern.
They have spent 15 years and £1.5m on the fight.
stories.why_it_matters: The ruling strengthens protection for a rare wetland and shows that determined action can defend wild places from lasting damage.
